historyReviewBoundary: All 115 histories have author source checks. Final independent review covered metadata and numerical checks for all 115 classes, 12 deeper class targets and source-gap samples in seven classes. It did not independently verify every passage of every cited source.

history.name: Organic nitrate vasodilators

starting.description: Brunton witnessed experimental vascular effects of amyl nitrite and reported angina relief; Murrell connected nitroglycerin's physiological effects to that comparator and predicted benefit. Separately, prior sugar-alcohol nitrate depressor effects prompted the Krantz laboratory to study sugar-anhydride nitrates, including an isosorbide nitrate.

inspiration.description: Experimental vascular and clinical effects of amyl nitrite, physiological effects of nitroglycerin, and known depressor effects of sugar-alcohol nitrate compounds supplied starting observations in different episodes. Amyl nitrite is a nitrite comparator, not a nitrate class member.

steps.description: Brunton combined observed amyl-nitrite effects on arterial tension with an angina case and reported pain relief after a deliberate therapeutic test.
Murrell connected nitroglycerin's physiological effects with amyl nitrite and anticipated benefit in angina, then compared their pulse tracings.
Murrell described relief of anginal episodes after administering dilute nitroglycerin.
The 1939 anhydride-nitrate series included table-named isosorbide dinitrate tested for blood-pressure effects in dogs (E6).
Carr's retrospective dates a report to 1940, but the named compound was already reported in 1939; Silber separately dates synthesis to 1938. Exact synthesis priority remains unresolved.

A separate historical abstract describes Porjé's Swedish research on isosorbide dinitrate and marketing in Sweden in 1946, without establishing the initiating idea or its connection to the U.S. studies.
A mononitrate was reported as an in-vivo dinitrate metabolite in 1967; isosorbide-5-mononitrate was described as an active metabolite in clinical use by 1990.

design.description: Murrell deliberately compared physiological responses and clinically tested a dilute solution of an already available compound. The Krantz laboratory then prepared a different series of sugar-anhydride nitrate structures for pharmacological investigation, rather than merely changing delivery.

circumstances.description: Murrell's angina trial followed a stated physiological analogy; the 1939 laboratory's synthesis and pharmacological study of anhydride nitrates followed prior depressor observations. This describes these deliberate research stages, not every finding or a blanket absence of chance.

limits: Amyl nitrite is a pharmacological comparator outside the assigned organic nitrate class.

The 1939 table names isosorbide dinitrate; its printed chemical diagram and direct lineage to later clinical preparations were not independently verified. Isomannide dinitrate was the authors' selected further-study compound.

The intellectual starting point of Porjé's Swedish isosorbide program and its relationship to the earlier Maryland work are not stated in the abstract consulted; do not transfer the Maryland rationale to it by assumption.
The clinical introduction of isosorbide-5-mononitrate is established by the 1990 review, but the developers' specific original rationale is not established by that review.
conflicts: S3 already names and studies isosorbide dinitrate in 1939, qualifying Carr's S5 statement that it was reported in 1940. Silber S4 dates synthesis to 1938; Berlin S6 describes a later independent U.S. synthesis. The unread full retrospective and underlying synthesis records leave exact priority and reconciliation unresolved.
gaps: The indexed original pp. 187–190, including Table 1's compound name and dog-assay text, were reopened in final review. Direct PDF/page-image access and independent verification of the chemical diagram remain unavailable.
Carr's full 1985 retrospective and the report he assigns to 1940 remain unread; exact synthesis priority and the 1938/1939/1940 chronology are only partly reconciled.
Berlin's full review and the original Swedish development account were not read; the Swedish program's initiating idea remains unestablished.
The original clinical-development account establishing why isosorbide-5-mononitrate was introduced has not been located in full text.

humanContributionInterpretation.summary: Angina relief with amyl nitrite and comparative physiological effects informed Murrell's nitroglycerin treatment.
humanContributionInterpretation.scope: Brunton's earlier bleeding observation also informed the nitrite hypothesis; later isosorbide branches have distinct experimental histories.
